data.current_summary: Create a watch
data.current_description: Free to create. Adds a target to the Watchlist. Where the plan includes the collection section, a watched event's imagery is then checked automatically at 1 token a day per watch, until before and after scenes are found or 14 days after the first report; a day without enough tokens is skipped and not charged, and on other plans imagery is not checked and nothing is charged. target_type "event": pass the signal's id (uuid) as event_id — the server resolves and binds the CANONICAL event (never an article URL), so further reporting and even a later cluster merge stay on the same watch. target_type "area": pass a bbox — created as a saved bookmark; to measure something there use POST /api/v1/monitoring, to watch its events use POST /api/v1/standing-orders (both join the same watch automatically). target_type "site": watch a specific place for change — a registry facility (entity_id from GET /api/v1/entities/search) or any point (lat, lon) — at a scale: "facility" (radius 250 m–3 km; measured from imagery by default when the kind of facility has a suggested measurement, e.g. vessel counts for a port), "city" (radius 5–20 km; measured only when you pass a metric) or "country" (followed through reporting only; never measured). Linked events are reported with how they were linked (named / nearby / country). A refused explicit metric creates nothing; a refused default is reported in `measurement.reason`. Measuring uses a monitored-area slot and costs the same as POST /api/v1/monitoring. Active watches are plan-limited; re-adding an existing target returns the existing watch (200) instead of consuming a slot.

data.current_description: Costs 3 token(s) per request — the same as a page of signals. Takes no parameters: every strait and canal where ship transits are measured (28 places — Hormuz, Suez, Bab el-Mandeb, Malacca, Bosporus, Panama, Taiwan Strait and others) is returned in one response, the places outside their usual range first. Each place carries status — usual, below or above its usual range, or not_measured — and level, an index computed by this product: the 7-day average of ship transits with the usual level set to 100 (index), the change against usual (change, 0.05 = +5%), the same index for tankers alone (tanker_index), and revised when the underlying figure changed after it was first recorded. Two kinds are returned. kind=facility: a heat source of at least 10 MW within 2 km of a registered facility — a refinery, power plant, port, base, dam, bridge and the like; airports are excluded — that is at least 5 times the strongest detection within 500 m of the same spot in the 21 days before (or where none was detected). kind=night_source: a night-time heat source of at least 20 MW with no registered facility within 2 km, at least 5 times its own spot's 21-day maximum and 3 times that of the surrounding 10 km, compact and with little burning around it; its facility and distance_m are null, and it does not rule out vegetation fires. Each record states what was measured — strength, time, satellite, the earlier level, and for kind=facility the distance to the facility — and never a cause: a detection does not distinguish an attack, an accident, flaring or a vegetation fire, and the heat source may be outside the facility. data.current_summary: Transit anomalies: ship transits at straits and canals against their usual level
data.current_description: Costs 3 token(s) per request — the same as a page of signals. Takes no parameters: every strait and canal where ship transits are measured (28 places — Hormuz, Suez, Bab el-Mandeb, Malacca, Bosporus, Panama, Taiwan Strait and others) is returned in one response, the places outside their usual range first. A transit anomaly is a measurement, not a report. Each place carries status — usual, below or above its usual range, or not_measured — and level, an index computed by this product: the 7-day average of ship transits with the usual level set to 100 (index), the change against usual (change, 0.05 = +5%), the same index for tankers alone (tanker_index), and revised when the underlying figure changed after it was first recorded. Ship counts are not returned. Usual level: the median of the 7-day averages over the 12 weeks before. A 7-day average is outside its usual range when it is statistically unusual against those weeks (modified Z-score of 3.5 or more) and at least 15% away. meta.definition carries the same sentence. While a place is outside its usual range, anomaly gives the direction, since (the first day of the current unbroken run, looking back 30 days), days, and event_id — the event recorded for it, the same id GET /api/v1/signals returns with categories=transit_anomaly (measured=true, measured_kind=transit), so the event endpoints work on it; null when no event is linked. entity_id is the registry id GET /api/v1/entities/{entityId} takes, which returns the recent levels of one place. It never states a cause: weather, holidays, a closure, an attack and re-routing all change the number of ships. The measure comes from ship tracking (AIS) signals and covers container, dry bulk, general cargo, ro-ro and tanker ships, so ships that do not broadcast, and other kinds of vessel, are not counted. The underlying measurements are updated weekly, so a change becomes visible 4 to 11 days after it happens; meta.as_of is the latest day measured. The numbers (index, change, tanker_index, revised) need a plan with the full event detail. Without it every place still returns its status, anomaly and event_id, with detail_withheld=true and null in those fields (meta.detail_included and meta.detail_required_plan say so).

data.current_summary: Night-light anomalies: city night lights below half of their own usual level
data.current_description: Costs 3 token(s) per request — the same as a page of signals, and the same plan window applies (meta.window_clamp says when it was cut). A night-light anomaly is a satellite measurement, not a report: on a night, the lights measured over one of a fixed list of cities were below 50% of that city's own usual level (NASA Black Marble, VIIRS). A night is judged only when at least 70% of the city's box could be observed; the usual level is the median of the most recent earlier such nights (at least 5, at most 30). Nights of one continuing drop are one record (a new record starts after a judged night that was not a drop, or a gap of more than 3 days). Each record carries the city (name, country, centre and the half-size of its box), night (the latest night of the drop, a UTC date), first_night and nights (every drop night in the record), ratio_to_usual and percent_of_usual (0.41 / 41 = 41% of the usual level), observed_share (how much of the box was observed that night), baseline_nights, product (the Black Marble product, e.g. VJ146A2_NRT), granule (the product file the value was read from) and provisional. provisional=true means the value came from the near-real-time product and can change when the standard product arrives about nine days later. The nightly brightness values themselves are not returned. Every record is also an event (same event_id as GET /api/v1/signals with categories=nightlight_anomaly, where it carries measured=true and measured_kind=nightlight), so the event endpoints work on it. related_events lists events tied to this one by a stored relation — nothing is inferred when the record is read, so it is usually empty; it needs a plan with event relations (otherwise null, and meta.notes says so). The detail — which city, the level against usual, the nights, the observed share and the summary — needs a plan with the full event detail. Without it every record still returns that it was recorded, when, the position and its kind, with detail_withheld=true, a placeholder title and null in the withheld fields (meta.detail_included and meta.detail_required_plan say so); the same records in GET /api/v1/signals carry the placeholder title too. cities lists every monitored city on every page, whether or not it has a record — it is not filtered by bbox, dates or cursor: slug, name, country_code, lat, lng, status (usual = the latest judged night was within the usual range; below = the latest judged night, no more than 3 days old, was below 50% of the usual level; not_judged = neither can be said, and reason says why), level (the latest judged night: night, ratio_to_usual, percent_of_usual, observed_share, provisional), nights (the last 30 days, newest first; ratio_to_usual is null on a night that was not judged) and baseline_nights. Join cities[].slug to a record's city.slug. A city marked usual states a measurement of one night, not that nothing happened there; the nightly brightness values are not returned for cities either. For cities, a plan without the full event detail gets every monitored city (slug, name, country_code, lat, lng) with status, reason, level, nights and baseline_nights null and detail_withheld=true — which city is below its usual level is part of the detail. meta.definition carries the thresholds, meta.notes what the record does and does not establish, and meta.attribution the source credit, which must be shown with the data. Cursor pagination via meta.next_cursor.
